scope: Proposition 3.5 (Low-dimensional preparation) of the manuscript “Sharp logarithmic exponents for fixed off-diagonal Ramsey numbers” (preprints/Sharp-Logarithmic-Exponents-for-Fixed-Off-Diagonal-Ramsey-Numbers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 170 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 20ab597a1d3dea22), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose (3.1) holds with j ∈ {2, 3} and n = |S| ≤ |T|. Either enumeration already proves Lemma 3.1, or the following preparation costs O(q + σ) bits. In dimension three there is also a possible reduction to the dimension-two description lemma, with the same final cost, size, capture, and failure bounds as Lemma 3.1. In the case not resolved by enumeration or that reduction, we have n > 100qP, a retained set S′ ⊆ S of size n′ ∈ [n/2, n], and either an empty list or an ordered plane list Π1, . . . , ΠJ in PG(3, q). In the latter case the sets Ci = (S ∩ Πi) \ [ h<i Πh (1 ≤ i ≤ J) (3.8) partition S′, have nonincreasing sizes, and satisfy |Ci| < .04n′. The decoder knows the list and all cell sizes, but need not know S′ or the cells themselves. Write n = q1+v , g = (v − 1/2)σ, χ = P/100, χ0 = P/10000, B = qj /n′ . (3.9) For every ambient query point x, define Ox to be the cell Ci of its earliest containing listed plane, and Ox = ∅ if there is none. Define fx = |Ox|/n′ ≤ .04, Xx = S′ \ (Ox ∪ {x}). (3.10) If no list is present, Ox = ∅ for all x. When j = 3 and g > χ0, the preparation additionally ensures either (i) every plane meets S′ in fewer than Kp = n4/3q−1e−g/5 points and the list is empty; or (ii) the list is present and J ≤ n/Kp = q1/2e−2g/15.
